issues.quote: Monnier had made us all show our watches, as he does every year, and told me my case wanted cleaning and my hands were a disgrace.
issues.fact: The fact sheet says nothing about watches being shown, compared, or set at dinner, and gives no reason to doubt Girard's watch.
issues.misreading: A solver could take this to mean the watches were checked against each other or set to a common time, or that Girard's watch was inaccurate. Either reading would change how the 'by my watch' readings should be trusted.

issues.quote: I did not play cards with him tonight and I was glad of it.
issues.fact: The fact sheet gives no information about Girard's dealings with Dr Vauthier or about any card game.
issues.misreading: A solver could read this as a claim about where Vauthier was, or as a hint that the doctor was occupied elsewhere during the evening, which the sheet does not support.

issues.quote: He owes me money. A sum I will not name in front of his aunt. I am not ashamed to say I wanted to see him about it.
issues.fact: The fact sheet says only that Girard went up to Félix in the library at 10:46 by his watch. It gives no debt, no purpose for the visit, and no aunt.
issues.misreading: The added motive and the mention of a debt could be taken as established facts about why Girard went upstairs, which may bear on what he did between his return to the house and his meeting with Félix.
